colours._how_to_read: hex = rendered sRGB in the best-lit plain patch. These renders are graded much less warm than the work-room set (the walls render #beaa98 here vs #85674a there). hex_white_balanced applies per-channel linear gains that make the shaded white radiator in p03 (#a59689) neutral (R x0.913, G x1.004, B x1.10). Use hex_white_balanced as a starting base colour under ~3000 K lights, or hex under neutral light.

notes: CEILING HEIGHT: with square pixels and the plan's horizontal dimensions the bedroom renders put the ceiling at 2.539 m (joint fit; each render with a floor edge alone gives 2.534-2.540), not the owner's 2.40 m and not the work room's 2.608 m. The ceiling pocket on the balcony wall rises to 2.61, so the render model has a ~2.61 m slab with a ~7 cm dropped ceiling in this room. All heights in this file are in that render-model scale.
The door A leaf top measures 2.057 m (casing top 2.136), not the owner's standard 2.00 m; the work-room door measured 2.075.

Adapting to 2.40 m (owner decision needed): either keep absolute heights for things with real-world sizes (bedside tables 0.30-0.50, bed, armchairs, radiator, TV 1.28-1.91, handles, doors) and re-anchor the ceiling-hung items to 2.40 (wardrobe top panel, wall panels, LED lines, pendant canopies, pocket), or scale every y by 2.40/2.539 = 0.945. The balcony-door heads (2.41) and shutter boxes cannot fit under a 2.40 ceiling, so they need a decision.

Openings: C and E are both full-height single-leaf glazed balcony doors (a mirror pair, handles on the TV-pier side at about 1.06 m). The bedroom has no window, and the radiator is not under an opening: it sits on the wall pier between the doors, under the TV. Plan item B is the split AC unit; plan item D is the TV with the radiator below it.

All six cameras are outside the room (p01 behind the wardrobe, p02 and p03 behind the headboard wall, p04 in the top-right wall corner, p05 behind the top wall, p06 beyond the balcony). Reproduce them with camera.near set to near_clip_m, or by hiding the walls behind the camera.

Camera accuracy: shared focal 2026 px (hfov 64.6 deg, vfov 50.7 deg; the work-room set used 1965 px, so the lens differs). Edge reprojection rms is 0.3-1.4 px per camera (0.86 px over 166 residuals). A variant with a focal length per camera gives 2018-2066 px and moves positions by under 4 cm. Pitch is -0.8 to -5.5 deg, roll under 0.1 deg. If the scene is built with a 2.40 m ceiling, keep the camera heights (1.43-1.53 m) as heights above the floor.

Bed, armchairs, side table and rug are measured from partial views: bed +-3 cm, armchairs and side table +-10 cm, rug x min hidden under the bed. The armchair seat height (0.45) and the side-table diameter are assumed.

Could not be determined: the headboard-wall panel thickness, the frame depth of the balcony doors in their reveals, the sash details of door E (only partly visible), and what the notches along the balcony's outer edge in the plan are. The balcony railing heights assume the railing stands at the outer edge.

No curtains or interior blinds appear in any render; the roller blind mentioned in docs/room-notes.md is the external roller-shutter box above each balcony door. The ceiling pocket on the balcony wall is empty.

Colours are rendered pixel values; see colours._how_to_read. This set is graded far less warm than the work-room set, so materials that appear in both rooms (floor, wardrobe doors, walnut) should share one base colour rather than copying each room's rendered hex.
